PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework from Song, Song, Pfister, and Yoon, published as arXiv:2604.05018 on April 6, 2026, and presented at the Third Conference on Language Modeling (2026). It turns unconstrained pre-writing materials into publication-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including literature synthesis and generated plots and conceptual diagrams. The authors say existing autonomous writers are rigidly coupled to specific experimental pipelines, and produce superficial literature reviews.

The pipeline has five agents: outline generation, plot generation, literature review, section writing, and content refinement. The outline agent produces a JSON plan covering visualizations, a literature search strategy, and citation hints. The section-writing agent drafts the remaining core sections. A refinement loop reverts to the previous version if the overall score drops.

Reported results are mostly from side-by-side human evaluation against AI Scientist-v2. Those results show an absolute win rate margin of 50%-68% in literature review quality, and 14%-38% in overall manuscript quality. The abstract's headline 90%–99% win rates refers to a different comparison, so the two figures should not be conflated. Citation counts are also reported as 45 to 48 references on average, closely tracking the 59 citations in human manuscripts.

Caveats: the arXiv and Google Research pages are the primary sources. The rest of the results are secondary summaries and community skill-pack sites, and their agent names vary slightly from the paper's. I did not open the full PDF, so the figures above come from search snippets.
